We find that the observed nuclear suppression in Drell–Yang dilepton production in E866 experiment at E lab = 8 0 0 GeV can be explained well by the parton shadowing effect in nuclear medium as parametrized in EPS08, and the effect of partonic energy loss in the beam proton is negligible.

the initial state effects on DY lepton production in proton–nuclear collisions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nuclear modification of DY spectra in the E866 experiment at Fermilab E lab = 820 GeV is mainly due to parton shadowing, but the initial parton energy loss effect may be significant at low x and at low x ′, and the final-state multiple gluon radiation in DY process is negligible.

the observed nuclear suppression in the DY cross section at Fermilab energy is mainly due to parton shadowing, while at lower proton energy, the suppression can be explained by both parton shadowing and beam parton energy losses.
the nuclear suppression of Drell–Yann cross sections observed by E866 experiment at E lab = 820 GeV can be well described by parton shadow in target nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parton shadowing and parton energy loss are two important mechanisms for understanding nuclear suppression of Drell–Yann process in p + A and A + A collisions.
the observed nuclear suppression in DY lepton pairs in the kinematic range as covered by the recent E866 experiment can only be understood if the effect of partonic energy loss is negligible.

the nuclear suppression in Drell– Yan process in p + A at Fermilab energy is dominated by parton shadow effect in target nuclei, but the initial parton energy loss effect becomes important for DY lepton pair with large x ′ and small x.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nuclear suppression of the Drel–Yan cross sections in p + A collision can be understood in terms of the nuclear modification of the parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the target nucleus and the beam parton PDFs, which are induced by the initial-state parton energy loss.
the nuclear suppression of DY dilepton spectra is dominated by parton shadow in target nucleus and the contribution of beam quark energy loss is negligible at the FermiLab energy E lab =800 GeV.
